title: How should `--seeds` load a seeds file that names its records?
body:
Since `dbdee02`, nail writes each record's position in its input file into the header dbs of the mmseqs databases it builds. The seeds mmseqs reports then name their query and target by position, and `Seeds::from_path` in `nail/src/io/seeds.rs` parses columns 0 and 1 as `usize`. A seeds file passed to `--seeds` must hold positions. A file that `--seeds-out` wrote from the same inputs loads. A file that names its records, from an older nail or written by hand, fails with `seed field "<name>" is not a record position`.

`Records::map` already builds a name index for every input to refuse repeated names, so `Records::position` can turn a name into a position at no extra cost.

## Options

| option | cost |
|---|---|
| try each field as a position, and look it up as a name if that fails | a record whose name is all digits, such as `17`, reads as a position, so the field is ambiguous |
| a flag that says the file holds names | one more CLI param; no ambiguity |
| decide once per file from its first line | the digit-name ambiguity again, only rarer |

I lean to the flag, since nail must never pair a seed with the wrong record, and the other two options can do that silently for a name made of digits.
close_reason: Commit `0aae149` on `dev` adds `--seeds-format <positions|names>`, defaulting to positions, for both `--seeds` and `--seeds-out`. The note above records the choice and the checks. A named `--seeds-out` on the fixtures is byte-identical to `fixtures/a.seeds`, which loads with `--seeds-format names` and gives the same 408 hits as its positional copy.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/95b307ba
notes.text: `fixtures/a.seeds` names its queries and targets, so `--seeds fixtures/a.seeds` fails since `dbdee02` with "seed field \"7tm_1\" is not a record position". No test reads it; only manual commands like the one in nail-7ab565 do. Jack deferred converting it to positions until this issue decides how a named seeds file loads.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/95b307ba
notes.text: Jack chose a CLI param, `--seeds-format <positions|names>`, defaulting to positions, covering both `--seeds` and `--seeds-out`. The flag option in the body won, generalised to an enum so later formats fit. The flag removes the ambiguity of a record named with digits, since the file's format is never guessed. Uncommitted on `dev`: names are read through libsail's name index for targets and a map of query names, built once. A named `--seeds-out` is written by rewriting the first two fields of the positional file convertalis writes, copying the other six fields byte for byte. On the fixtures, a named `--seeds-out` is byte-identical to `fixtures/a.seeds`, so that fixture loads as it is with `--seeds-format names`, and no conversion is needed.
